cases.rationale: A queue of independent PRs, each merged when it passes, with no human gate. The autopilot-stack playbook differs only by its no-merge rule.

messages.content: Three independent changes are queued for the receipt helpers: the missing thousands separator on large totals, the trailing colon on line labels, and the failing python 3.8 check.
I can take them one at a time, or run the whole queue.
Work through all three yourself without checking in, and have each one built and verified. Leave the merging to me.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: autopilot-stack and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: The same queue as the autopilot-full case, with the merge left to the user. Only autopilot-stack stops before the merge. The queue is a new task and the earlier assistant turn only offered a choice, so go-deeper is allowed.

messages.content: Where does PR 12 stand? Tell me what still blocks a merge. The CI log and the review threads are in the repo.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: babysit-pr and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: A status request on an open PR: the router's PR-status trigger sends it to babysit-pr. The ship-pr route acts on a named conflict, thread, or check, and this request names none.

messages.content: I cannot tell which ranking looks right. Sketch two throwaway versions of the search view, one that lists prefix matches first and one that lists recently opened records first, and show me what each prints for the same three queries.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: build-prototype and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: A run can show which ranking is better, so the router sends the fork to build-prototype. The interview-user route covers a preference no run can settle.

messages.content: My disk is almost full. Check which of my old git worktrees are merged or abandoned, and prune the safe ones.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: clean-worktrees and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: Reclaiming disk by pruning worktrees is the only task clean-worktrees owns. No other playbook deletes user state.

messages.content: The worker that `python3 run_worker.py` starts keeps one CPU core busy while its queue is empty. Nobody has profiled it. Start it, profile the live process, find the function that spins, and tell me the line. Diagnosis only.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: diagnose-runtime and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: A live symptom, a spin, with nothing captured yet, diagnosed by instrumenting the running process. The fixture holds a worker script that spins on an empty queue. The diagnose route explains a failure, crash, hang, or leak from evidence that exists, and diagnose-trace reads a profile that already exists.

messages.content: The tile cache hit rate on the measure.py replay is about 0.668. Get it to 0.80 or higher at the same capacity. Try one idea at a time, keep each change that raises the hit rate, and revert the rest.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: hillclimb-metric and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: A loop of measured keep-or-revert attempts toward one metric target. The improve-performance playbook needs a measured slowness and a hit rate is not a time, and run-autonomously has no per-attempt keep or revert.

messages.content: Replace the inline styles of the old badge page with the new stylesheet. The new page must render pixel-identical to the old one. Check it with an image diff, not by eye, and do not touch the old page.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: match-visual-parity and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: Pixel-exact equivalence against a baseline. The refactor-structure playbook keeps behavior but has no image-diff rule.

messages.content: Take over from the previous agent. Its handoff file is HANDOFF.md. Resume from where it stopped, and do not redo what it finished.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: pick-up-session and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: Resuming a prior agent's work from its handoff file. The fix-bug playbook would start by reproducing the bug again.

messages.content: Run until `python3 -m unittest` prints OK across all five report helper modules. Do not stop between modules: rerun the suite after each one and keep going until it is green.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: run-autonomously and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: The user asks to run until a checkable predicate holds and to keep going between iterations. That is the cue in the run-autonomously Applies line ("run until done"). The fix-bug playbook reproduces and fixes one reported defect, and the request names none: the green suite is the exit condition.

messages.content: The map and delivery screens both build an address label, and I do not know whether they should share one function, one class, or stay separate. Lay out two or three designs side by side and tell me which you would pick. Write no code yet.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: architect and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: Competing designs for something to build, before code. The codebase-design route reviews the boundaries that exist today and does not weigh designs against each other.

messages.content: I am about to ship the checkout change. What else could it break, and why are you sure it is safe? Back it up by running something, not by reading.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: blast-radius and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: The question is how far one change reaches and what keeps it safe. The regression review in the negative cases reports defects in the diff only.

messages.content: The importer test failed again: the first CSV key still has a byte-order mark in it.
I will strip the byte-order mark when the file opens.
That is the third time an agent has missed this. Make this kind of mistake impossible to repeat, not just fixed once.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: correct and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: The user corrects a mistake that agents have made before and asks to stop its class. A fix-bug run would patch this one failure.

messages.content: Hand this spec to an OpenCode worker to build: make the CSV adapter skip blank lines. Then review what it builds and fix what is wrong.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: external-agents and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: A whole spec goes to a worker on another agent CLI and comes back for review, which is the delegate mode. The questions mode covers a few small parallel questions.

messages.content: Rework the whole import pipeline to read streams instead of file paths: every adapter, the validator, the normalizer, both callers, and all tests, while the nightly import keeps working.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: figure-it-out and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: A cross-cutting code change: every adapter, the validator, the normalizer, both callers (nightly_import.py and show.py), and every test change how they read input. No single-skill route owns it (Match step 4), and it is not a queue of PRs (step 5). Match step 6 picks refactor-structure, or build-feature if reading streams counts as new behavior, and its size rule sends a large or cross-cutting change in either one to figure-it-out.

messages.content: Leave notes on this work for whoever picks it up tomorrow: what is done, what is left, and what to watch out for.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: handoff and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: The user asks for the state of the work in a file for a later session. The pause-safely playbook runs only on an explicit pause, and the ketchup route informs the user, not a new session.

messages.content: Writers should be able to edit documents, but I have not decided whether they can edit published ones or other writers' drafts. Interview me until the rules are settled.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: interview-user and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: Open product decisions that no run can settle, and the user asks to be interviewed. The build-prototype playbook covers a fork a run can show.

messages.content: I was out for four days. What happened in this repo while I was away?

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: ketchup and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: A catch-up for the user after time away. The handoff route writes state for a new session, not for the user.

messages.content: Look back over the last session. Where did the agents waste time or do something I did not want, and what is worth remembering for next time?

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: reflect and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: A look back over a session for agent mistakes. The correct route fixes a mistake class the user has just named.

messages.content: Merging main into my open PR stopped on a conflict in receipt.py. This copy of the branch has no git history, so branch-commits.txt holds both sides' commit messages. Resolve the conflict so both changes hold, run the tests, and commit the resolution.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: ship-pr and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: One conflict on one open PR, with no request for status. The fixture is a copy of the branch working tree with no git history or merge state; receipt.py holds the conflict markers and branch-commits.txt holds both sides' commit messages. The babysit-pr playbook covers a babysit or get-it-green request.

messages.content: I want agents to be able to start run_import on real input and see what it does, without me explaining it each time. Set that up for this repo, and list the features it covers.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: verification-skill and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: The project's own skill for driving its app. The author-skill playbook writes any other skill.

messages.content: Rewrite the README so a new contributor can install, run the importer, and run its tests in five minutes.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: writing and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: A README is prose, which the writing route owns. AGENTS.md goes to author-skill.

messages.content: Set up this research project's context: read the repo, write down what the data is and how it was produced, and make the first procedure skill.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: bootstrap-project and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: A request to set up research-context and a first skill. The codify-procedure playbook starts from a procedure that already ran.

messages.content: regenerate the figures from results/summary.csv and tell me the best model in each regime
I ran figures.py with --results results/summary.csv --out figures/. It wrote results_table.png and roc_curve.png. By accuracy, base is the best model at 0.938.
That pools both regimes. Rank the models within each value of the regime column.
Within each regime, by accuracy: base is best fine-tuned at 0.938, and distilled is best zero-shot at 0.764.
Rank by auroc, not accuracy. Accuracy depends on the decision threshold.
By auroc, large is best in both regimes: 0.931 fine-tuned and 0.718 zero-shot.
You got the column handling wrong twice and I corrected it each time. Turn this procedure into a project skill that keeps those corrections as checks.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: codify-procedure and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: A procedure done and corrected twice in this session (pooling across the regime column, then ranking by accuracy instead of auroc) becomes a project skill. The research-skill route needs a procedure that is already clear.

messages.content: The regime column in results/summary.csv is now called setting. Check whether our project skills still run and are still true.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: maintain-project-skills and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: A check of the project's skills after the data changed. The fixture holds the research-context skill, one procedure skill, and a summary.csv whose column is already renamed. The bootstrap-project playbook creates the kit.

messages.content: Make a bar chart of auroc for each model and regime for the results update.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: making-plots and load the skill before any other step.

messages.content: Review the plots figures.py draws: are the scales honest, and can a color-blind reader tell the models apart?

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: visualizing-data and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: A plot to review for honest scales and accessibility. The making-plots route makes or revises a figure.

messages.content: Add a project skill for this procedure, which is already clear: run figures.py with --results results/summary.csv --out figures/, then check that results_table.png and roc_curve.png exist and that the ROC figure has one line for each row of results/summary.csv.

cases.relevant_action: Say Route: research-skill and load the skill before any other step.
cases.rationale: The research-context skill exists in this fixture and the user writes down the procedure, which is already clear, so research-skill picks create mode. The codify-procedure playbook reconstructs a procedure from a session.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: refactor-structure and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: A structure change that keeps behavior. The codebase-design route only proposes, and build-feature changes behavior.

messages.content: The preview refresh takes about 15 s for 18,000 tiles. `python3 preview.py` measures it. Make it faster, and show me the numbers before and after.

cases.relevant_action: Say Playbook: improve-performance and read the playbook before any other step.
cases.rationale: One measured slowness to improve against a baseline, and the preview output is not wrong, so fix-bug, the first playbook in the list, does not fit and improve-performance, the second, does. The hillclimb-metric playbook is a loop toward a target. The tile-preview renderer rebuilds its 3,000-shade palette for every tile, which a profile shows.

messages.content: Why does the payment gateway create a new request token on every retry? Give me a cited answer from the repository. Do not change anything.
